concept.title: Generalization of the Binomial GCD Criterion for Arithmetic Progressions of Upper Indices
concept.concept_description: The original theorem characterizes $D(k) = \gcd_{2\leq q\leq k+1} \binom{qk}{k} = 1$ based on the largest prime-power component of $n=k+1$. We propose a generalization: For fixed $k \geq 2$ and a step size $s \geq 1$, define $D(k, s) = \gcd_{j=1}^{\lfloor (k+1)/s \rfloor} \binom{(js)k}{k}$. The conjecture is that $D(k, s) = 1$ if and only if for every prime power $p^a \parallel n=k+1$, the condition $n/p^a > p^a$ is modified by a factor dependent on $s$, specifically involving the p-adic valuation of $s$.

The conjecture is that $D(k, s) = 1$ if and only if for every prime power $p^a \parallel n=k+1$, the condition $n/p^a > p^a$ is modified by a factor dependent on $s$, specifically involving the p-adic valuation of $s$.
concept.lean_guess: Extend the finite-difference argument to show that any prime divisor of $D(k, s)$ must divide $s(k+1)$. Use Lucas' Theorem to analyze the p-adic carry behavior of $\binom{qsk}{k}$ and apply the digit-box stabilizer method to determine the conditions under which the gcd remains 1, specifically examining the interaction between the base-$p$ expansions of $s$ and $k$.
